head: a3063366a
mode: read-only source review; this artifact is the only write
goal_limit: Approve only a truthful, deterministic presidential REQUEST-OP selector repair. This review does not establish physical delivery, capture, checkpoint 707, calibration improvement, package correctness, or campaign acceptance.

prior_artifact_check.clarification: The earlier final correctly said no files changed. No earlier PREIMPLEMENTATION_CANON_REVIEW artifact existed; this follow-up creates it under the owner-designated directory.

authority_applicability.ruling: The regular presidential Request-op is governed by the ordinary CorpsOperation minimum and participant ceiling. Systems Manual section 21 does not create a two-brigade or unbounded exception and expressly says the presidential note does not supersede sections 6.4, 7.5, or 8.

citations.effect: Request-op is a strategic directive through generals; the additive presidential note does not supersede section 6.4.
The president names strategic intent, never brigades or axes; Request-op reuses the merged staging/injection substrate. It is not classified as an authored historical operation.
The injected request is constructed with isPrePlanned=false and type sector_attack.
Ordinary sector-offensive launch criteria include at least three brigades.
A corps operation assigns up to 12 brigades; the corps commander draws them from the full corps pool.
The phase authority delegates operation preparation to Systems Manual section 7.6 and supplies no Request-op roster exception.
Request operations remain in the normal War operation lifecycle; the War specification supplies no minimum-two or unbounded exception.

code_contradictions_to_correct_in_this_p.current: planDirectiveOperation reuses AUTHORED_OP_MIN_PARTICIPANTS=2 for a non-preplanned sector_attack
code_contradictions_to_correct_in_this_p.ruling: Use a directive-local regular sector-attack minimum of 3. Do not change AUTHORED_OP_MIN_PARTICIPANTS or authored, triggered, queued, opportunity, or bot paths.

code_contradictions_to_correct_in_this_p.current: planDirectiveOperation admits every available brigade with no ceiling
code_contradictions_to_correct_in_this_p.ruling: Cap this regular directive at 12. Do not alter the separate generic sector_offensive.ts cap or tune unrelated operation paths.

selection_policy.rule: After existing availability, cross-operation commitment, live-formation, enclave-objective, and friendly-route guards, rank candidates using the established generic sector-attack commander comparator: equipment offensive priority descending via getEquipmentOffensivePriority(resolveEquipmentClass(formation)), then strictCompare formation ID. Take at most 12, then store/return the selected participant IDs in strictCompare order for canonical output.
support: src/sim/combat/sector_offensive.ts lines 2721-2738 already uses equipment priority descending with strictCompare tie-break for ordinary sector-attack participants.
src/sim/combat/sector_offensive_launch_helpers.ts lines 95-107 exposes the pure equipment priority and equipment-class helpers.

Using strictCompare-sorted pool.slice(0,12) alone would create an unsupported semantic preference for lexicographically small formation IDs; the established equipment comparator avoids that invention.
Do not copy the generic 15 percent reserve slicing. Reserve retention is a separate allocation mechanism and is not stated by the Request-op authority.

test_files: tests/op_directive_staging.test.ts only if an existing hard-guard assertion needs a direct regression extension
required_reuse: an existing pure normal friendly/allied route or connected-component helper
forbidden_expansion: No bot, authored, triggered, queued, opportunity, generic sector_offensive, combat predictor, combat threshold, alliance, supply, control, movement execution, save schema, CA cost, or UI brigade-picking change
No distance, radius, roster-size below 12, personnel-at-admission, or objective-priority heuristic
No direct location/control mutation, forced flip, teleport, or brigade diversion outside an admitted CorpsOperation

planner_contract.shared_purity: Keep planDirectiveOperation as the single pure plan used by queryDirectiveObjection and injectOpDirectives.
planner_contract.staging: Sort friendly adjacent staging candidates with strictCompare and choose the first candidate for which at least three legal route-capable formations exist. This preserves the existing lexicographic staging tie-break while making it feasibility-aware; it adds no distance optimization.
planner_contract.participants: For the chosen staging cell, select only available, uncommitted, active same-corps formations allowed for the target objective and connected by the normal friendly/allied route. Apply the established equipment-priority comparator, cap at 12, then canonicalize returned IDs with strictCompare.

rejections.objective_unreachable: No friendly adjacent staging cell exists.
rejections.no_available_force: Friendly staging exists, but no candidate staging cell has at least three legal route-capable formations.

planner_contract.force_over_objection: A forced request may override commander advice only. It cannot bypass objective, route, enclave, availability, minimum-three, maximum-12, validation, or slot guards.

enclave_gate.ruling: A distinct historian review is mandatory because the repair changes operation eligibility for Srebrenica/Žepa-tagged formations, even though it reuses the existing predicate unchanged.
enclave_gate.panel_scope: A full section 6 panel is not automatically required. Escalate only if the historian identifies a reward-for-atrocity issue, a dispute, or another bright-line question under lines 222-233.

determinism_and_compatibility.ordering: Sort staging candidates, comparator ties, final participant IDs, and corps traversal with strictCompare. Reverse insertion order must not change the plan.
determinism_and_compatibility.headless: Preserve injectOpDirectives lines 861-864: with no pending_op_directive, return before planner invocation and perform zero mutation.
determinism_and_compatibility.save: Add no GameState or IPC field. Planner-local sets/maps/components and ephemeral ranking are not serialized. Existing pending_op_directive shape and desktop serialize-autosave-broadcast ownership remain unchanged.
determinism_and_compatibility.query_consume_parity: The objection query and consume step must receive the same plan for the same state and adjacency.

red_first_fixture_plan: First RED in tests/op_directive_objection.test.ts: 3-12 route-capable objective-legal formations plus a disconnected regular and an enclave-illegal formation; expect only legal routed formations, equipment-priority selection where relevant, strict final ID order, and byte-identical JSON before/after planner call.
RED: lexicographically first friendly staging neighbor has fewer than three legal routed formations while the second has at least three; expect the second staging cell.
RED: friendly staging exists but every candidate has fewer than three legal routed formations; expect no_available_force. No friendly neighbor remains objective_unreachable.

RED: more than 12 legal routed formations with differing equipment classes; expect exactly 12 chosen by established equipment priority then strict ID tie-break, with final participant output strict-sorted.
RED determinism: reverse formation object insertion and adjacency-neighbor insertion; expect identical plan.
Injection RED: forced_over_objection with a hard planner failure injects nothing and records the same rejection; a legal plan injects exactly the planned participants.
Preserve the existing no-pending headless zero-mutation and planner purity assertions.
unresolved_outside_scope: src/sim/combat/sector_offensive.ts currently declares a code-level participant cap of 20 while canon says 12. This review does not authorize or assess a global generic-operation correction.
No result from focused selector fixtures can establish real movement delivery, capture causality, 707, or campaign parity.
implementation_authority: The owner's broad authorization for recommended ordinary-player capability fixes covers bringing this Request-op path into existing canon. No canon document or acceptance criterion is changed.
